newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady, unruffled by auction.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady, unruffled by auction.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were mostly steady, holding in fairly well despite a late rally in bond prices after a so-so Treasury auction, dealers said.
"It (volatility) has been at couple-month lows over the last couple of days, so it's not going much lower," a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade said.
Nor was there much inclination to bid up volatilities ahead of a long weekend, traders said, particularly as the market appeared to be digesting this week's new Treasury issues without much trouble.
U.S. financial markets will be shut on Monday due to the Presidents' Day holiday. On Friday, interest rate products on CBOT and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange will close early.

Implied volatility for June T-bond futures options ended virtually unchanged from Wednesday at around 9.7 percent. March volatility was off half a point to about 8.1 percent, but March options expire next week and the bid-ask spread was as wide as half a point, dealers noted.
"It's a dead issue," an investment bank trader at the CBOT said of March implied volatility.

The $10 billion 30-year bond auction today, the third and final leg of the Treasury's quarterly refunding, produced an average yield of 6.640 percent and a stop of 6.660 percent, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.42 times.

The numbers were in line with the market's expectations. March T-bond futures fell from early afternoon highs immediately after the results came out but soon rallied back up to close at the highest level since the end of last year.
Traders expect volatilities to stay lackluster for a while, perhaps until Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony at the end of February.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, expected March futures to see a few weeks of sideways consolidation after perhaps making another push higher on Friday toward 113-1/2 to 114.

Grauer, who earlier in the day predicted today's late rally based on 60- and 100-minute stochastics, said the daily stochastic was in the last stage of a bullish divergence and needed to refresh itself. In doing so, he noted, the daily, weekly and monthly stochastics will all have made a fresh upcross by early March, setting the stage for a strong rally.
"It will be the first time in a long time that all three are in confluence," he said.
Fading fears of an imminent credit tightening also subdued volatilities for the shorter end of the yield curve.
Implied volatilities for Eurodollar futures options were narrowly mixed, with June and September virtually flat at 8.8 and 12.4 percent respectively.
A brokerage trader at CME said there had been a notable increase this week in spreads with strike prices right next to each other, often fairly deep out-of-the-money.
He noted that such trades were probably aimed at reducing exposure to time decay while taking advantage of the historically low volatility levels
